transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Thank you, doctor. It's, um, it's really nice of you to see me. I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need, because it's... well, it's probably nothing too serious. 

But I just keep messing up these little things. Just small details, you know? Like, um, I'll be at the senior center and I'll write down the wrong time on a class sheet. Or I'll be out working on a project and measuring a board—I'll measure it once, but then I still end up cutting it a hair short just because I sort of skipped over the small print on the tape. 

It's nothing major, really, just a little embarrassing when people notice. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking for.
Have you struggled with these kinds of details throughout your life, or is this a more recent change?

Well, um... I guess it's always been there, if I'm being completely honest. I hope it's okay to bring up stuff from way back then, but, well... even when I was just a little boy in elementary school, it was kind of the same story. 

My teachers, they were always very kind about it, you know? They would write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, which was nice of them to say. But they'd also mention that I'd forget my books, or, um, somehow misplace my homework on the way to school. And I guess I had a habit of just... staring out the window, watching the birds or the cars go by, unless someone tapped my desk to keep me on track. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be a bad student or anything! I just... drifted a bit. I hope that's not too silly to mention at my age. Does that help answer your question?
Growing up or even now, have you ever felt restless or had trouble sitting still?

Well, um... I really try not to be a bother to anyone, so I wouldn't say I'm bouncing off the walls or being disruptive. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest, sitting still for a long stretch can be a little tricky for me. 

Like, if I'm sitting through a whole meeting, or even just having a quiet evening at the condo, I start to get this... well, sort of an ants-in-my-pants feeling? I just get this sudden urge to get up and check on something, or maybe just putter around the room for a minute. I always try to do it quietly, you know, maybe offer to get someone a glass of water, just so I don't disturb anyone else's evening. 

It's just a little extra energy, I suppose. I hope that's what you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or finishing their sentences before they have a chance to finish?

Oh, goodness, no. I really try my best to be a good listener. I would hate to be rude or make anyone feel like what they're saying isn't important. 

I mean, I suppose everyone gets a little eager to chime in sometimes, right? But I always try to wait my turn. If I ever did talk over someone, I'd feel just terrible about it and apologize right away. I really value what other people have to say. 

I hope that's alright? I try very hard to be polite, you know.
